title: How Do Airlines Actually Make Money?
description:
Delta's credit card deal with American Express paid it $8.2 billion in 2025, more than the airline's entire profit. Here are the three places the money really comes from.
#delta #airlines #money #shorts

Sources: Delta Air Lines full-year 2025 results (Jan 13, 2026); Fortune (Jan 2026); AltexSoft (Jan 2026); AP via WABE (2024); CBS News and TravelMole, citing Bureau of Transportation Statistics data for 2024
Photos: ST33VO, frankieleon, DeltaNewsHub, KrzysztofTe Foto Blog (CC BY 2.0, Flickr); D Coetzee (CC0, Flickr)
first_comment: Be honest: do you pay for checked bags, or cram everything into a carry-on? 🧳

scenes.say: A credit card company paid Delta {$8.2 billion|eight point two billion dollars} last year. That's more than Delta's whole profit.
scenes.source: Delta FY2025 results, Jan 13 2026 (Amex remuneration $8.2B; GAAP net income $5,005M); AltexSoft Jan 2026; Fortune Jan 2026

scenes.say: Delta's profit was about {$5 billion|five billion}. The card money was way bigger.
scenes.source: Delta FY2025 income statement (net income $5,005M; pre-tax $6.2B); Amex remuneration $8.2B (Delta release; Fortune; AltexSoft)

scenes.say: So how does an airline actually make money?
Number one: credit cards. Every time someone swipes a Delta Amex, Delta gets a cut.
scenes.source: AP via WABE 2024 ('The money comes from the fees AmEx collects from the billions of dollars spend on the cards'); Delta FY2025 release (growth driven by co-brand spend)

scenes.say: Delta's own earnings report says that money grew eleven percent last year.

visual.quote: American Express remuneration in 2025 grew 11 percent to $8.2 billion, driven by double-digit growth in co-brand spend in each quarter of the year.

scenes.source: Delta Air Lines press release, Jan 13 2026 (ir.delta.com), verbatim; same text in the 8-K exhibit

scenes.say: Number two: your bags. U.S. airlines made over {$7 billion|seven billion dollars} on checked bags in {2024|twenty twenty four}.
scenes.source: CBS News citing BTS (about $7.27B in 2024); TravelMole ('more than $7 billion on bag fees in 2024')

scenes.say: Number three: the big seats. Delta's premium sales grew {7%|seven percent} last year.
scenes.source: Delta FY2025 release ('Premium revenue grew 7 percent year-over-year'); Fortune Jan 2026

scenes.say: Regular economy? Its CEO says it hasn't really moved.
scenes.source: Fortune Jan 13 2026 (Ed Bastian: 'we have not really seen Main Cabin move yet'); Reuters via AOL Jan 2026 (main-cabin ticket revenue fell 7% in Q4 2025 while premium rose 9%)

scenes.say: Cards, bags and big seats. That's how an airline really makes money. And it's why
